_id: clk016 -- towerClocksInEkfRubidiumDatum. clock rung: the ESTIMATOR ARCHITECTURE axis, third and predicted-best cell. clk014 (OCXO datum) and clk015 (caesium datum) between them proved that tower-clock estimation on one-way GEO is stable behind a pinned datum and that its cost is set by the DATUM OSCILLATOR rather than by the architecture. This rung completes the sweep with the oscillator that should be best on both of the axes that matter here. Read clk016 against clk004 (oscillator match, broadcast product) and against clk015 (architecture match, worse datum clock).
_delta: ARCHITECTURE SWEEP 3/3. Against clk015 the single change is clock.tower.clockType, CESIUM1 -> RUBIDIUM. Against clk004 the changes are the same two architecture leaves clk014 and clk015 carry, clock.mode -> 'includeTowerClocksInEKF' and clock.gauge.mode -> 'fixReferenceTower'.
_prediction:
PRE-REGISTERED, written before the run. Rubidium should win this axis outright, and for TWO independent reasons that happen to point the same way.

(1) The PRODUCT-RESIDUAL axis, which is what clk003-clk005 measured: clk004's mechanism predicts RUBIDIUM at ~4.9 mm uncorrected residual at the 20 s mean product age, against CESIUM1 at ~0.30 m and OCXO at ~1.09 m, because JOW's caesium is white-FM dominated with h0 = 1e-19, three orders above rubidium's. This axis sets what the BROADCAST partner achieves.

(2) The DATUM-WANDER axis, which is what clk014 and clk015 exposed: pinning x(b_twr1)=0 forces b_rx to absorb the tower-1 random walk, and that walk is random-walk-FM driven, i.e. governed by hMinus2, where OCXO is worst (2.51e-22) and rubidium is better than caesium. This axis sets what the ARCHITECTURE costs.

So the quantitative expectation: clockBiasRMS_runwide_m should fall below clk015's 2.99692, positionClockErrorCorr should retreat from clk015's -0.65713 towards clk004's value, and the position penalty against the broadcast partner should be smaller than clk015's 1.9 percent. arcNisOverallPerDof should stay consistent, near clk015's 0.910757 rather than clk014's 3.72618.

THE INTERESTING WAY THIS COULD BE WRONG: clk004 is the strongest broadcast rung on the whole clock axis precisely because rubidium's product residual is millimetric. If the broadcast product is already at ~4.9 mm there may be nothing left for the states to absorb, in which case clk016 would show the architecture's costs (datum leak, initial transient) with none of its benefit, and could be the WORST cell of the three relative to its own partner even while being the best in absolute terms. That would sharpen the overall conclusion rather than blunt it: state augmentation helps only where the product is poor.
_result:
MEASURED 2026-08-18, 3600 s arc, 3601 epochs, run_oo_v1 from the live tree, same MC caveat as clk014 and clk015, and the same six-figure finalAttitudeError_deg agreement (0.0167507) across all six cells.

THE PREDICTION WAS HALF RIGHT, AND THE HALF THAT FAILED IS THE INTERESTING ONE. _prediction's stated quantitative expectation was that rubidium would win on both axes. On the DATUM-WANDER axis it did, exactly as the hMinus2 argument said: clockBiasRMS_runwide_m 2.71708 against clk015's 2.99692, the smallest absolute datum leak of the three EKF cells. But the headline expectation, a SMALLER position penalty than clk015's 1.9 percent, FAILED outright. The measured EKF-vs-broadcast penalty per oscillator pair is OCXO +17.96 percent, caesium +1.91 percent, rubidium +15.48 percent. Rubidium is the WORST cell relative to its own partner while carrying the best absolute datum. That is precisely the outcome _prediction flagged as 'THE INTERESTING WAY THIS COULD BE WRONG', pre-registered before the run: clk004's broadcast product is already millimetric (clockBiasRMS_runwide_m 0.0832448, the best of all six cells), so there is nothing left for the states to absorb and clk016 pays the architecture's costs with none of its benefit.

THE FINDING THAT ONLY THE FULL 2x3 COULD SHOW, and it is stronger than anything the individual cells said: THE ARCHITECTURE IMPOSES A POSITION FLOOR THAT IS BLIND TO THE GROUND OSCILLATOR. The three EKF cells land at finalPositionRMS_m 2.49989 (OCXO), 2.07977 (caesium), 2.07404 (rubidium), and run-wide at 4.98784, 4.45944, 4.45603. The caesium and rubidium EKF cells are the same number to three figures. The three BROADCAST cells, by contrast, spread across 2.11932, 2.04079, 1.79598, i.e. the oscillator is a real lever there. So putting the tower clocks in the EKF DESTROYS THE VERY LEVER the clk003-clk005 sweep was built to measure: once the ground clocks are states, buying a better ground oscillator stops paying. Anyone reading the clock axis for a procurement answer must be told this, because it inverts the axis's whole premise. positionErrorMax_m makes the same point structurally: 14.08 for all three EKF cells and 13.7135 for all three broadcast cells, oscillator-blind on both sides, which confirms the peak is the 1000 m P0 tower-clock transient from ScenarioFactory.towerClockInitSigmas_ and not physics.

WHITENING IS GENERAL, WHICH SETTLES _watchThis. arcNisCarrierLag1 goes 0.173498 -> 0.0187104 for rubidium and 0.186895 -> 0.00718733 for caesium, with arcNisCarrierNEff 2536.21 -> 3468.72 and 2466.93 -> 3549.61. Rubidium's broadcast product was ALREADY clean and the states still whitened it by an order of magnitude, so the absorption is a real mechanism and not merely the removal of a large product staircase. Note what this means taken together with the position result: the states genuinely absorb the correlated tower-clock error, the innovations genuinely become white, AND THE SOLUTION STILL GETS WORSE. Innovation whiteness is not a proxy for accuracy here. arcNisCodeLag1 is untouched at 0.31987 (clk004 0.314181), consistent with the standing result that the residual correlated budget is multipath colour rather than clock.

CONSISTENCY HOLDS: arcNisOverallPerDof 0.892346, carrier 0.960017, code 0.719143, i.e. the caesium result generalises and only the OCXO datum breaks the covariance.

VERDICT ACROSS THE FULL 2x3, which supersedes the per-rung verdicts in clk014 and clk015: on one-way GEO at G5S1R4 a pinned-datum tower-clock EKF is STABLE and STATISTICALLY CONSISTENT for any ground oscillator except OCXO, it WHITENS the carrier innovations below what any broadcast product achieves, and it is NEVERTHELESS DOMINATED BY THE BROADCAST PRODUCT ON ACCURACY AT EVERY OSCILLATOR, by 1.9 to 18 percent, while additionally costing a 2.7 to 3.0 m clock datum and flattening the ground-oscillator lever to zero. The recommendation is unchanged from the default: keep clock.mode='spacecraftReceiverClockOnly'. What changes is the REASON. honestCovarianceConfig.m:87-104 says do not enable it because it diverges. It does not diverge when the datum is pinned. Do not enable it because it is dominated, and because it removes the ground-segment lever the clock axis exists to measure.
_watchThis: The number carrying the real finding across this sweep is arcNisCarrierLag1, not position. clk005 sits at 0.186895 and clk015 at 0.00718733, i.e. the tower states whiten the carrier innovations BELOW what the broadcast product achieves. Against a millimetric rubidium product clk004's lag-1 should already be low, so clk016 measures whether the whitening is a real absorption mechanism or merely the removal of a large product staircase. If clk016 whitens further still, the mechanism is general.
_trap: All traps from clk014 apply unchanged and are not restated: 'externalTowerCorrections' appends ZERO gauge rows under this clock mode (measured) and leaves the datum unpinned; deterministic=false is load-bearing; hardware.txCodeBias.useInEKF and the ISL four-timestamp path both THROW under estimateTowerClocks=true. See clk014's _trap for file and line references, and clk014's _datumWarning, which applies here too: this rung's clock column sits on a different datum from clk001-clk013 and is not comparable to them.
_combination: space = CESIUM1  |  ground = RUBIDIUM (stochastic)  |  h-table = jowTable2p1 (inherited)  |  architecture = tower clocks IN the EKF, datum pinned at tower 1  |  paired against clk004 (oscillator match) and clk015 (architecture match)
